sentences.text: A degraded mode is entered when a fault, communication loss, environmental limit, or external restriction prevents normal service without requiring immediate full-site shutdown.
The system records the affected function, the detected condition, and the time of transition so that operators can assess the scope and duration of the impairment.
Safety functions take priority over energy production, maintenance throughput, and schedule recovery in every degraded mode.
Turbine Controller retains protective control locally when the supervisory connection is unavailable, while the Shore Control Room monitors the loss of visibility.
If remote commands cannot be confirmed, the Control Engineer suspends those commands and uses approved local procedures until reliable control is restored.
The Weather Service and Weather Analyst support entry into Weather Hold when forecast or observed conditions exceed approved operating limits.
A turbine with a safety-critical fault is placed in Turbine Lockout until the fault is assessed and the required work is authorized.
The Offshore Substation enters Substation Degraded when a protection, auxiliary supply, or monitoring impairment limits safe switching or export capability.
The Grid Interface Relay applies the configured response to a Grid Constraint, and the Grid Dispatcher is advised when generation capability changes.
Marine activity is reduced or suspended in Vessel Standby when weather, visibility, communications, or vessel capability is insufficient for safe transfer.
The Marine Coordinator and Vessel Master confirm that personnel and vessels can remain safely accounted for during an extended interruption.
The Fire Detection Panel and Emergency Generator remain essential services during degraded operation and are not bypassed to recover production.
The SCADA Gateway preserves available status and alarm information, while the SCADA Engineer investigates missing or inconsistent indications.
The Fleet Dispatch Console presents operational restrictions so that the Duty Planner can prioritize urgent safety work and maintainable generation capacity.
The Maintenance Planning Engine separates safety-critical work from tasks that can safely wait until normal access and support are available.
The HSE Officer reviews any proposed workaround that changes established access, isolation, or personnel-control arrangements.
A degraded condition is escalated when its duration, uncertainty, or effect on adjacent equipment increases beyond the approved operating envelope.
The Control Engineer coordinates technical recovery with the relevant field and shore roles before any protection or operating restriction is removed.
Recovery begins only after the initiating condition has been corrected or bounded and the responsible operator has confirmed that the equipment is stable.
Required inspections and functional checks are completed before affected equipment is returned to automatic control or normal duty.
The SCADA Engineer verifies that status, alarms, and command feedback are consistent across the available control views.
The Duty Planner updates operating priorities and deferred work after the recovery status is confirmed.
Normal service is restored in stages so that a successful response at one level does not conceal a remaining restriction elsewhere.
The system retains the event record and recovery decisions for review, trend analysis, and improvement of operating procedures.
